key_insight: SymFT speeds up fault-tolerant quantum circuit simulation by separating symbolic Clifford/Pauli frames from the small set of non-stabilizer degrees of freedom that actually affect sampling.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical, high-throughput simulator for error-correction and near-Clifford workloads where many shots are dominated by stabilizer structure, making large-scale benchmarking and protocol development cheaper.
method: Symbolic Clifford--Pauli frame factorization keeps residual Clifford/Pauli operations symbolic so they do not need to be applied every shot.
Adaptive stabilizer-coordinate planning uses a shared tableau to define the basis and stores only active non-stabilizer coordinates in a compact dense vector.
Direct multi-coordinate sampling instructions avoid per-shot tableau updates and localization-induced Clifford transformations.
evidence_signal: On tested pure-Clifford and near-Clifford circuits, SymFT outperformed Stim by 2.51–2.56× on surface-code circuits, outperformed Clifft by 1.86–3.51× on cultivation and distillation circuits, and beat SOFT by more than two orders of magnitude on tested cultivation circuits.
watch_item: The approach relies on efficient basis planning and symbolic frame handling, so performance may depend on circuit structure and the cost of managing dynamically changing active coordinates.
paper_title: SymFT: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuit Simulation via Symbolic Clifford--Pauli Frames and Stabilizer Coordinates
